verdict_reason: This is a framing consultation on two measurement designs, not an acceptance or diff review, so the verdict is advice only.
reply_markdown:
## Framing - challenged first

- **No single denominator spans both vendors.** Astra's binding resource is a shared, time-gated window; GLM's is money. Score within vendor and publish per-vendor tables; a cross-vendor "winner" is meaningless.
- **Window share is the wrong denominator even for Astra.** The window is account-wide: it moved 8 to 72 % with no C3 run at all (state.md 11:57) and 30 to 65 % nonlinear inside one run (09:02). Per-run window deltas charge other consumers' spend to the reviewer. Denominator: the run's OWN input tokens (ledger `tokens`, cached counted); window share stays a feasibility gate ("expected share per round at this effort"), never the score.
- **Two designs the brief does not list.** (a) **epsilon-exploration**: track-record routing starves itself - a tier that starts unlucky never gathers evidence; route ~10 % of low-stakes purposes (chore, checkpoint, framing) to the less-proven tier; the roster policy is a prior, not a rule. (b) **Escalation ladder**: reading passes go out at medium and re-send at high only when the reply is unusable or findings=0 on an acceptance purpose - cheaper than always-high and it manufactures the medium-vs-high pairs the score needs.

## Q1

gpt-6-astra: chore low; framing/decision/checkpoint medium; diff-review high (nine rounds, one real defect each, 10-15 % of a window); acceptance high; core-contract/stuck xhigh. glm-5.3 (real tiers: low/high/max): chore low; checkpoint/framing/review high; stuck max. Score: confirmed findings (alternative 3, once the join exists) per million run-input tokens; usefulness marks as the interim numerator. "Is medium enough" is answered in weeks by epsilon-exploration plus RC2, not by months of passive events.

## Q2

SubagentStop is the right point - per worker, zero model tokens - with caveats: it fires per stop and SendMessage continuations re-stop one agent (dedupe on a minted `worker_ref`, consult_ref-shaped, and count resumes); the payload likely lacks model/effort (RC1) - take the model from the transcript's init events (closed list), effort from the transcript when present, else from `workers rate --effort`, and record `effort_source` so the rated-only subset's bias is visible; duration from transcript timestamps, not a start hook.

Must stay out: anything not a class or a count - transcript/session ids and paths, agent names as typed (closed tier list only), briefs, prompts, tool outputs, file contents, edit diffs, environment values, and the state.md sketch's `--note` (free text; keep it in the local findings store).

Attribution under rework: never infer it - the coordinator marks a closed `disposition` at wave close (kept | reworked | discarded | superseded) against `worker_ref`; "useful" then means "the wave kept part of this worker's output", which survives rework.

## Q3

Publish now, all closed: `effort` (tier sent), `effort_requested` (the PRE-mapping tier of the same vocabulary - the preset name alone loses it, and zai-v1 collapses medium to high), `effort_source` (preset|policy|flag|native), `tokens_cached` (cached input counts against the window), `panel_role` (solo|scout|judge|shadow - a scout's "useful" is not a judge's). Worker event: `worker_ref`, tier, model (closed list), effort, effort_source, outcome, duration class, resumes, edits (read-only|writes), verified, disposition. Caveat: `close_event` rejects every event_type but consultation|rating (classes.rs:869) - allowlist, constructors and intake must learn `worker` in the same wave as the hook ships.

## Q4

It fails three ways: the digest is lossy compression tuned to the obvious (it drops the one-line defect inside a big hunk); scout and judge of one model family share blind spots (GLM low to GLM max); a judge that cannot see omissions cannot audit the digest. Caps: the judge ALWAYS receives the complete diff stat (cheap, makes omissions detectable); cap the summary (~300 words), never the evidence - verbatim hunks up to a byte budget, each omitted hunk listed by path and size, truncation marked, the scout's hypotheses separated from quoted lines.

## Requested checks

- **RC1** Temporarily register a `SubagentStop` hook that writes stdin to a file (Claude Code settings), spawn and continue one subagent, inspect the payload's keys. Any directory; workspace-write; 15 min; settles finding #5.
- **RC2** Two consultations, same pinned brief and range, `-Effort medium` vs `high` on gpt-6-astra; compare findings and ledger tokens/quota. Working dir: repository root; workspace-write; budget ~2 x 15 % of one 5-hour window; settles Q1's medium question.
- **RC3** `curl -s <z.ai OpenAPI/docs URL for glm-5.3>` and read the reasoning-effort enumeration. Read-only; 10 min; settles whether z.ai exposes more than three tiers.

findings.claim: No telemetry event carries the effort or the cached-token count today, and the sketch's two fields (effort = tier SENT, effort_requested = preset name) cannot recover the requested tier: zai-v1 maps medium to high, and a roster effort policy or -Effort override changes the tier without changing the preset name - so the planned per reviewer x effort table would merge two populations on the z.ai side and hide the policy's effect everywhere.
findings.trigger: A glm-5.3 run requested at medium (preset, policy or flag) and one requested at high: both leave as effort=high with identical effort_requested, forever indistinguishable in the intake.

evidence.observation: Details and RatingDetails have no effort or cached-tokens field; the allowlist is the plugin's 0.6.1 shape.
vocabulary_map zai: low/high/high/max - medium and xhigh both collapse.
-Effort (low..xhigh) overrides the purpose preset, so the preset name does not determine the requested tier.

findings.verification: Run one z.ai consultation at -Effort medium and one at high and inspect the two spooled events: today both lack effort entirely; under the sketch both would read effort=high with no distinguishing field.
findings.remedy: Publish three closed fields now - effort (sent tier), effort_requested (the pre-mapping tier in the same none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max vocabulary), effort_source (preset|policy|flag|native) - plus tokens_cached as the cost side.

findings.claim: Scoring a tier by usefulness per 5-hour-window share attributes other consumers' spend to the reviewer: the window is account-wide, moves without any C3 run, and is nonlinear in the run's own tokens.
findings.trigger: Any scoring interval that overlaps another consumer of the ChatGPT account (observed 8->72 % between 11:18 and 11:55 with no C3 runs; 30->65 % inside one 260k-token run).

evidence.observation: The 11:57 entry records the window moving 8->72 % without our runs; the 09:02 entry records 30->65 % inside one run for 260k tokens, nonlinear.
RunQuota.tokens carries the run's OWN input/cached/output (baseline-subtracted), while quota is the account-level window observation - the clean and the polluted cost measures are already separate.

findings.verification: Diff two consecutive ledger entries' quota.used_percent against their own tokens deltas on a day another Codex session ran: the share moved while the run's tokens did not.
findings.remedy: Use the run's own input tokens (cached counted) from RunQuota.tokens as the denominator; keep window share only as a feasibility gate (median share consumed per round at each effort tier).

findings.claim: close_event discards any event whose event_type is not consultation or rating, so a worker event queued before the allowlist, the typed constructors and the intake learn the third type is silently dropped (one local diagnostic line) - the hook must not ship in the same release that does not extend all three.
findings.trigger: A build ships the SubagentStop hook while its sender still runs the current closer: every event_type=worker body returns None and is counted as rejected.

evidence.observation: close_event returns None for any event_type other than consultation and rating; the doc comment says such a body is discarded with a local diagnostic.

findings.verification: Spool a minimal event_type=worker body and run the sender against a loopback test intake: the event is rejected/dropped and counted in the flush report.
findings.remedy: Extend close_event, the Event constructors and the intake schema for event_type=worker in the same wave as the hook, and gate the hook's installation on the bridge version.

findings.claim: The state.md worker-rate sketch carries `--note` (free text), contradicting the closed-class contract the same file states at line 149 (the intake's agent_report free text must NOT be reused); the handoff's cleaner `useful yes|partly|no` mark must win and the note must never reach the event.
findings.trigger: A user types a note naming a file, a path or a person: the closed-class event has nowhere to put it, so it either leaks or the field exists dead in the schema.

evidence.observation: Line 131 designs `c3 worker rate <id> yes|partly|no --note`; line 149 records the operator's own rule that free text breaks the closed-class contract and must not be reused.

findings.verification: Read the two sketches side by side (handoff 01 section B vs state.md:131): the note appears in one only.
findings.remedy: Keep the note in the local findings store only; the event carries the mark, rating_rev and judge exactly as the reviewer rating event does.

findings.claim: SubagentStop fires per stop and SendMessage continuations re-stop the same agent, so per-worker counts double without a per-worker pseudonymous id plus a resume count; and the effort is probably not in the hook payload or the subagent transcript, making effort-bearing rows a coordinator-rated (biased) subset.
findings.trigger: One logical worker continued twice: three SubagentStop events counted as three workers; effort rows exist only for workers the coordinator bothered to rate.

evidence.observation: The sketch has a resumes class but no per-worker id, and names the effort visibility in the transcript an open question with the rate command as fallback.

findings.verification: Register the dump-to-file hook of RC1, continue one agent twice, and observe repeated stop events plus which keys the payload carries.
findings.remedy: Mint worker_ref (a guid, consult_ref-shaped) at first stop, count resumes on it, and record effort_source: transcript|operator|none so the bias of the operator-supplied subset is visible in the table.

findings.claim: Scout-and-judge fails on lossy digests and correlated blind spots: a summary tuned to the obvious drops the one-line defect inside a large hunk; a scout and judge of one model family share blind spots (GLM low digest, GLM max judge); and a judge that cannot see what was omitted cannot audit the digest.
findings.trigger: A past range whose real defect (e.g. the wave-8i/8j instant-ordering bugs) lives in one line of a big hunk the scout paraphrased instead of quoting.

evidence.observation: The sketch gives the judge the digest plus a call cap and nothing else; no omission audit.
The reading discipline exists for exactly this failure mode (stat first, then hunks one path at a time) - the digest must not bypass it.

evidence.reference: the sketch's example pairings (GLM low scout, GLM max judge)
evidence.observation: Same-family scout and judge correlate errors; the brief's own quota lesson (a cold cache) is why the digest, not the diff, reaches the judge.

findings.verification: Run the scout-and-judge pair on a past range whose real defect is known (F62-1's wave) and check whether the digest carries the defective hunk verbatim or only a paraphrase.
findings.remedy: The judge always receives the complete diff stat; cap the summary (~300 words), never the evidence - verbatim hunks up to a byte budget with each omitted hunk listed by path and size, truncation marked, hypotheses separated from quoted lines; prefer a different model family for the judge than the scout.

unproven: Whether z.ai exposes more than three effort tiers on glm-5.3 (docs not checked; RC3).
What the installed Claude Code version's SubagentStop payload actually carries (model, effort, agent_transcript_path); RC1.
Whether gpt-6-astra at medium finds the defect classes that high finds - needs the RC2 A-B run.
Whether the intake's published tables and the t-hub client contract can gain a third event_type and new detail keys without breaking the published schema (the server-side contract was not read here).
